It should be noted that approximately one minute after removal from the plasma chamber, the bond strength of any exposed areas is drastically reduced and most likely will not bond. As a result, the bonding procedures should be completed immediately to ensure adequate bonding. Furthermore, since both the glass and PMA are easily detachable after initial contact, the tolerance of the interface holder should be carefully evaluated such that both PMA is easily removable. For a four-inch diameter PMA, one percent tolerance allows for a satisfactory fit to hold, bond, and release the PMA after bonding procedures.

A testing bed for the PMA platform can be fabricated with digital switching boards (ULN2803 board, Elexeol), solenoids (S070M-6BG-32, SMC), a controller (typically a NI-DAQ or an Arduino), and vacuum and pressure lines along with a manifold or barbed fittings for interfacing with the chip. Fig. 6A shows an example of a testing bed. steps.title: Fabricate pneumatic and fluidic molds
steps.instruction: Design fluidic and pneumatic layers in AutoCAD, print photomasks, and perform soft‑lithography on two 5‑inch silicon wafers: dehydrate at 95 °C, spin‑coat SU‑8 2050 to ~80 µm (pneumatic) and ~50 µm (fluidic), pre‑exposure bake 10 min at 65 °C then 16 min at 95 °C, UV expose at 240 mJ/cm² (UV KUB2), post‑exposure bake 5 min at 65 °C then 10 min at 95 °C, develop 4 min, hard‑bake 150 °C for 30 min, then measure geometry with a surface profiler and inspect under a microscope.

steps.title: Apply parylene coating to fluidic mold
steps.instruction: Coat the fluidic SU‑8 mold with parylene‑C to a thickness <1 µm using a Specialty Coating Systems PDS 2010 and a silane A‑174 adhesion promoter; this surfactant layer eases PDMS release and provides visual damage cues.

steps.title: Prepare PDMS replica
steps.instruction: Mix PDMS base and curing agent 10:1, degas in a vacuum chamber, pour into the pneumatic mold bath (Fig. 2A) and degas again; during pneumatic degassing pour the remaining PDMS onto the fluidic wafer and spin‑coat at 200 rpm for 30 s to obtain a 200 µm thick film. Cure both layers overnight on a 45 °C hot plate (≈0.3 % shrinkage).

steps.title: Remove PDMS replicas from molds
steps.instruction: For the pneumatic layer, cut around the mold with a sharp knife, lever the PDMS off, wrap in plastic wrap and store. For the fluidic layer, place two PET sheets slightly larger than the mold, lay one sheet on the PDMS, lift the PDMS with flat‑tip tweezers, then perform a stretch‑relaxation peel (halfway peel, then lower) and place a second PET sheet on the exposed side before bonding preparation.

steps.title: Punch pneumatic access ports
steps.instruction: Attach double‑sided tape to a PDMS holder with a reference position, align using CNC punching system, register reference in software, punch 48 pneumatic and interface holes (Fig. 3B), cut the layer to size with a circle cutter, measure thickness at four locations for uniformity, then wrap in plastic wrap until bonding.

steps.title: Clean PDMS layers before bonding
steps.instruction: Fluidic layer: remove PET film, lift any trapped air bubbles, tape‑clean particles, tape‑clean the top surface, cover with a petri dish. Pneumatic layer: rinse in isopropyl alcohol, rinse in DI water, dry with N₂, dehydrate on a 45 °C hot plate, then tape‑clean.

steps.title: Practice alignment of layers
steps.instruction: Cool the pneumatic PDMS to room temperature, secure it on a vacuum chuck, place the fluidic PDMS on a motorized xyzθ alignment stage, view with a digital microscope (Plugable Technologies, USA), and verify at least two valves and two alignment markers on each end; if misaligned, repeat the stretch‑relaxation peel and re‑check.

steps.title: Plasma bond pneumatic and fluidic layers
steps.instruction: Expose both PDMS layers simultaneously to O₂ plasma at 80 % power, 7.5 sccm O₂ flow for 30 s; place the fluidic layer channel‑side down and the pneumatic layer channel‑side up in the chamber, spray briefly with N₂ after exposure, bring layers into contact, remove bubbles, then bake at 65 °C for 30 min to form an irreversible bond.

steps.title: Punch fluidic wells and interface holes
steps.instruction: Using the already‑punched pneumatic holes as guides, punch all fluidic wells and interface holes (Fig. 3B), double‑check critical positions, then perform a final clean (IPA rinse, DI water rinse, N₂ dry) and bake at 45 °C for ~10 min before wrapping and storage.

steps.title: Trim and verify assembled PMA
steps.instruction: Trim excess PDMS at the perimeter, remove the lower plastic cover, connect vacuum and pressure sources to all pneumatic ports, and test each microvalve for proper actuation; inspect under a microscope for contamination bridges or broken lines and troubleshoot as needed.

steps.title: Surface passivation via PFTCS stamping
steps.instruction: Create a tape mask with circles 0.1 mm smaller than the valves and scaled to 99.7 % of the design, cut with a Roland vinyl cutter, place on a 3 mm PDMS slab, tape the mask‑stamp assembly to the top of a vacuum desiccator, heat a block to 115 °C for ≥2 h, add 100 µL PFTCS to the lids of two microcentrifuge tubes, place the block and lids in the desiccator, pump to –80 kPa, seal and hold for 30 min. Remove the stamp, align it on the cleaned PMA using the motorized stage and digital microscope, press together with a 3 kg weight on a 150 °C hot plate for 30 min, then remove the stamp and store the PMA. Optional verification of PFTCS transfer can be done with a high‑resolution microscope or profilometer.

steps.title: Prepare glass substrate
steps.instruction: Submerge the glass in a piranha bath (2 H₂SO₄ : 1 H₂O₂) for 5 min, rinse briefly with DI water, dip in DI water for ~30 s, dry with N₂, dehydrate at 95 °C for 10 min, then cool to room temperature.

steps.title: Bond PMA to glass
steps.instruction: Place the glass in a wafer holder with a lip, optionally tape the PMA perimeter (avoid microvalves), expose both PMA (fluidic side up) and glass to O₂ plasma (same 80 % power, 7.5 sccm, 30 s), dry briefly with N₂, align the PMA on the glass using the holder (or, for featured glass, use an interface holder with posts that fit the interface holes), bring into contact, push out any bubbles, and bake at 65 °C for 30 min. Note that bonding must be completed within ~1 min after plasma exposure.

steps.title: Assemble testing‑bed hardware
steps.instruction: Set up a testing platform with a ULN2803 digital switching board, S070M‑6BG‑32 solenoid valves, a controller (NI‑DAQ or Arduino), vacuum and pressure lines, and a manifold or barbed fittings to interface with the PMA.

steps.title: Perform general QA of assembled PMA
steps.instruction: Open all microvalves and visually inspect for sticking; run a valve‑actuation sequence to transport fluid from inlet to outlet, observe any stuck or delaminated valves, and if needed place problematic valves under extended vacuum or fabricate a new chip with improved surface passivation.

steps.title: Validate pumping performance
steps.instruction: Execute the pumping sequence: open inlet valve, sequentially open the nine central valves, open outlet valve, then close the nine valves; measure flow with an SLI‑1000 (Sensirion) flow meter, integrate flow to obtain volume per cycle, compare to the theoretical displaced volume of ~95 nL (derived from Eq. 3 for 0.75 mm radius, 160 µm membrane thickness, 80 µm pneumatic height). Record efficiency (~85 %) and note actuation times required for different fluidic resistances.

steps.title: Demonstrate mixing capability
steps.instruction: Pump a green fluid into a storage well, then pump a red fluid into the same well using the programmed valve sequence; confirm mixing by the observed color change, optionally quantify with a fluorophore assay.

steps.title: Long‑term operation test
steps.instruction: Run the standard pumping sequence continuously for >20 h, monitoring flow rate and checking for bubble formation or delamination; confirm that performance and bond strength remain stable throughout the test.
